sections.what_happened: The European Parliament on Oct 22 voted 432-52-88 (88 abstentions) urging EU member states to consider an EU naval mission to protect Black Sea commercial shipping and asking NATO to examine a complementary initiative provisionally called 'Black Sea Sentry'. On Oct 23 a drone struck the Comoros-flagged cargo vessel Khoryv ~13 nautical miles off Constanta, Romania; it caught fire and sank: 1 sailor confirmed dead, 3 missing, 9 rescued (13 Ukrainian and Azerbaijani crew). Romanian President Nicusor Dan blamed Russia. EU Today tallies at least 8 commercial-vessel strikes in October with ~30 sailors dead or missing across the incidents (tally reported, not independently verified). This is a NATO-flank maritime escalation distinct from the Hormuz theatre; PortWatch does not cover the Black Sea as a chokepoint, so no PortWatch figure applies here.
sections.what_verified: EP official record + Romanian presidency attribution
sections.what_disputed: Russian attribution for Khoryv rests on the Romanian president's statement; no Russian response or independent forensic attribution is on record in-window. The '~30 dead or missing' October tally is an EU Today aggregation, not a wire-verified count, and the confirmed toll is considerably lower.
sections.why_matters: A second sea war is now on the parliamentary record: while Hormuz dominates headlines, the Black Sea just got a 432-vote call for an EU naval mission after a ship sank 13 miles off a NATO coast. Lead with the vote number, then the Khoryv's 13 crew.

totw_analysis: Our read: A second sea war is now on the parliamentary record: while Hormuz dominates headlines, the Black Sea just got a 432-vote call for an EU naval mission after a ship sank 13 miles off a NATO coast. Lead with the vote number, then the Khoryv's 13 crew. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Does the Black Sea need its own EU naval mission, or would 'Black Sea Sentry' drag NATO into a second maritime war?
